title: Marguerite and the Deadline
premise: Yara Whitlock, a financial-crimes investigator whose job is to make powerful people's dirty money look clean, is assigned to erase all traces of a private flight carrying a whistleblower. Mid-flight, every record of the plane vanishes from every system—including Yara's own—revealing that the network which trained them in laundering can also launder reality itself. As Yara digs into the vanished flight, they discover the network plans to legitimize itself at an upcoming global financial summit, and that the whistleblower aboard was someone Yara once loved. Hunted by former colleagues and haunted by their complicity, Yara must decide whether to stay invisible or burn the network from inside. In the end, Yara leaks everything at the summit at devastating personal cost, toppling the network but losing their name, their career, and any chance of a life untouched by what they've done.
about_author: Cyrus Galloway is the pen name of a former compliance officer who spent a decade inside the machinery of international finance before walking away with nothing but notebooks. Marguerite and the Deadline is his third thriller, drawn from cases he says he can neither confirm nor deny.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Yara Whitlock's POV. We meet them mid-task: scrubbing a senator's shell-company trail until it shines. The work is meticulous, soulless, well-paid. A colleague jokes that Yara could launder a saint. The emotional beat is quiet self-erasure—Yara has become very good at not existing.

chapters.title: The Whitlock Method
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Yara's POV: their recruitment years ago by the Meridian Group, the consultancy that taught them how money hides. Their mentor, Odile Marchand, praised their 'gift for making things never have happened.' The beat is seduction—how good it felt to be chosen.

chapters.title: Assignment: Marguerite
chapters.summary: Yara's handler delivers a routine job: expunge all records of a private flight code-named MARGUERITE departing Geneva. Standard cleanup. But the passenger manifest is sealed even from Yara, which has never happened before. Unease creeps in beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Forty Thousand Feet
chapters.summary: POV shift to Ilse Brandt, a forensic auditor aboard the flight, writing encrypted notes about what she's found in Meridian's ledgers. She's terrified but resolved, planning to land and testify. The beat is dread wrapped in courage; she addresses her notes to no one.

chapters.title: Vanishing Point
chapters.summary: Yara runs the deletion—and watches the flight vanish from radar feeds, booking systems, and air-traffic logs while it is still airborne. Not deleted: erased retroactively, everywhere, including backups Yara didn't know existed. Panic replaces procedure. Someone else got there first—or something bigger is operating.

chapters.title: Ghost Manifest
chapters.summary: Yara breaks protocol to reconstruct who was on board. Fragmentary records surface: seven names, six redacted, one legible—I. BRANDT. Yara recognizes the name and goes cold. The beat is recognition turning into vertigo: this is personal.

chapters.title: Ilse
chapters.summary: Extended flashback, Yara's POV: ten years ago, Ilse Brandt was the person Yara loved before Meridian recruited them both—and Ilse refused the offer. They parted as strangers on opposite sides of a line. Guilt and longing braid together.

chapters.title: No Such Flight
chapters.summary: Yara reports the anomaly to their handler and is told, flatly, there was no flight. When Yara pushes, their access credentials begin degrading in real time. The message is unmistakable: stop looking. The beat is the first open threat.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: A Meridian security man named Corben appears at Yara's apartment—not threatening, worse: friendly, offering a promotion and a warning in the same breath. He mentions Ilse's name once, softly. Yara understands they're being tested for loyalty.

chapters.title: Burner Protocol
chapters.summary: Yara begins building a shadow investigation off-grid: cash, burner phones, a storage unit. They pull a favor from Dev Okafor, a disgraced aviation-data analyst who owes them. The beat is cautious hope—the first time Yara chooses a side.

chapters.title: What Ilse Knew
chapters.summary: Decoding fragments of Ilse's recovered notes, Yara learns she'd traced Meridian's master structure: a lattice of foundations and sovereign funds designed to be presented at the upcoming Basel Integrity Summit as the world's cleanest capital pool. The network isn't hiding anymore—it's going legitimate.

chapters.title: Dev's Radar Ghost
chapters.summary: Dev finds a single uncorrupted ping from the flight's transponder over the Alps, then nothing. Either the plane landed somewhere unrecorded or it never landed at all. Yara refuses to say the word aloud. The beat is grief refusing its own name.

chapters.title: Odile
chapters.summary: Yara visits Odile Marchand, retired, in Lyon, hoping the woman who trained them will slip. Instead Odile is serene, almost maternal, and tells Yara: 'You were our best work.' The horror is affection weaponized; Yara leaves shaken and more certain than ever.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Yara realizes they're being followed—Corben's people, patient and professional. A near-miss in a Geneva tram tunnel forces Yara to abandon their apartment and go fully dark. The beat is adrenaline and loss: invisibility was supposed to be their craft, now it's their survival.

chapters.title: The Storage Unit
chapters.summary: Yara's safehouse cache is intact, but someone has left a printed photograph inside: Yara and Ilse, ten years ago, laughing. No note. The message is clear—we know your heart, and hearts are leverage. Fear curdles into fury.

chapters.title: Six Redactions
chapters.summary: Working the other six manifest names, Yara identifies two: a Meridian board member and a mid-level regulator—both now conspicuously promoted since the flight. The pattern emerges: the flight wasn't carrying witnesses to silence. It was carrying recruits.

chapters.title: The Offer Aboard
chapters.summary: Reconstructed scene from Ilse's notes: she was invited aboard to be offered a place in the new order. Her notes end mid-sentence over the Alps. Yara realizes Ilse said no at altitude, surrounded by six people who said yes. The beat is heartbreak sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Summit Countdown
chapters.summary: Twenty-two days to the Basel Integrity Summit, where Meridian's lattice will be ratified with regulators, banks, and press in attendance. After ratification, exposure becomes impossible—criticism becomes conspiracy theory. Yara sets the deadline: burn it before Basel.

chapters.title: Okafor's Price
chapters.summary: Dev agrees to help full-time but demands the truth about what Yara did for Meridian. Yara confesses in full—the accounts cleaned, the lives ruined indirectly, the craft of unmaking. Dev doesn't forgive, but stays. The beat is costly honesty.

chapters.title: Corben's Second Visit
chapters.summary: Corben corners Yara in a Zurich hotel bar and makes the real offer: come back, lead the summit's integrity unit, and Ilse's disappearance stays closed forever. Refuse, and Yara becomes the next record that vanishes. Yara stalls. Inside, they've already decided.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Using old Meridian credentials that somehow still work—someone is leaving doors open—Yara accesses the archive vault and photographs the master ledger linking the lattice to specific crimes: sanctioned oil, trafficked capital, a collapsed pension fund. The beat is triumph with a hook of doubt: why so easy?

chapters.title: Open Doors
chapters.summary: Yara realizes the accessible vault means either a trap or an ally inside. A breadcrumb—a dated memo in Odile's handwriting—suggests a faction within Meridian wants the summit stopped. Trusting it feels like stepping onto ice. Yara steps anyway.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: A dead-drop exchange with the internal faction: a former Meridian archivist named Tomas Reyes who believes the network betrayed its own founding rules. He gives Yara the final piece—the summit's ratification mechanism and its single point of failure. The beat is wary alliance.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Corben's team hits Dev's safehouse. Dev escapes with the data drives but is wounded; Yara must choose between retrieving the ledger copies and getting Dev to a hospital. They choose Dev, losing half the archive. The beat is sacrifice proving loyalty.

chapters.title: Half a Ledger
chapters.summary: With partial evidence, Yara approaches a journalist, Priya Nair, who once tried to expose Meridian and was destroyed for it. Priya is bitter, brilliant, and initially refuses: 'Partial ledgers get sources killed.' Yara offers themselves as the source instead. The beat is persuasion through self-exposure.

chapters.title: Naming Themselves
chapters.summary: Yara gives Priya a sworn account of their own crimes—every account cleaned, every name. It's both evidence of method and a suicide note for their old life. The beat is terrible relief: confession as strategy and penance at once.

chapters.title: Odile's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Odile summons Yara one final time and reveals she is the faction's author—the open doors, the memo. She trained Yara for this, she claims: 'I built you to break it.' Yara rejects the framing: they are not her instrument. The beat is severance from the maker.

chapters.title: The Trap Springs
chapters.summary: The faction contact was compromised weeks ago; Odile's gambit was real but Corben was watching her. Yara walks into a staged meeting and barely escapes, but Reyes is taken and Priya's office is raided. The ledger copies survive only because Dev split them. The beat is collapse.

chapters.title: Alone With It
chapters.summary: Dark chapter: Yara, hunted, injured, hiding in a freight yard outside Basel, weighs quitting. A memory of Ilse—her saying 'somebody has to keep the receipts'—rekindles resolve. The beat is the nadir and the turn.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: Basel fills with delegations, cameras, champagne. Meridian's ratification ceremony is tomorrow morning. Yara, Priya, and Dev map the venue: the evidence must reach the floor during the session, live, unspinnable. The plan requires someone inside with credentials—which means Yara using the identity they swore to bury.

chapters.title: Invitation Accepted
chapters.summary: Yara accepts Corben's old offer—summit integrity staff—as cover, walking back into the lion's mouth with the remaining ledger hidden in plain sight. Corben greets them warmly, certain he's won. The beat is icy performance: the liar's craft turned against its teachers.

chapters.title: Ilse's Receipts
chapters.summary: Dev decrypts the last fragment of Ilse's notes, recovered from the transponder buffer: she hid a complete copy of her findings in a Geneva safety deposit under Yara's childhood address. She planned for Yara to find it all along. The beat is devastating tenderness—love as contingency planning.

chapters.title: The Deposit Box
chapters.summary: Dawn run to Geneva and back, evading surveillance. The box holds Ilse's complete ledger plus a letter: 'If you're reading this, you chose. I always thought you would.' Yara grieves properly for the first time. The beat is love against duty, resolved into duty fueled by love.

chapters.title: Ratification Day
chapters.summary: The summit convenes. Meridian's chairman presents the lattice to applause. Yara stands at their integrity-staff post, watching the network become law in real time, waiting for the moment of maximum irrevocability. The beat is held breath.

chapters.title: The Floor
chapters.summary: Climax part one: during the ratification vote, Yara triggers the venue's document system, pushing Ilse's ledger, the master archive, and Yara's own sworn confession to every delegate terminal and press feed simultaneously. Chaos erupts. Corben sees Yara across the hall. The beat is detonation.

chapters.title: Corridor
chapters.summary: Climax part two: Corben corners Yara in a service corridor; a brutal, quiet struggle ends with Yara prevailing—but choosing not to kill him, leaving him bound with his own zip ties and his phone transmitting. Odile, watching from the gallery, gives Yara a single nod. The beat is victory without absolution.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Live
chapters.summary: The ratification collapses; delegations flee; arrests begin within hours as prosecutors who spent years unable to touch Meridian suddenly can't ignore broadcast evidence. Priya's story runs worldwide. Dev watches from a hospital bed. The beat is vertiginous vindication.

chapters.title: What Vanishes
chapters.summary: Inquiry chapters: Yara testifies, confesses again, and accepts prosecution for their own crimes as the price of the network's fall. Deals are struck; some principals walk; justice is partial, real, and unsatisfying. The theme lands: justice outside the law still costs the self.

chapters.title: Sentencing
chapters.summary: Yara pleads guilty to financial crimes and obstruction. At sentencing, they speak Ilse's name into the record—the first public acknowledgment she ever existed. Reduced sentence, but real. The beat is accountability embraced rather than endured.

chapters.title: Marguerite, Revisited
chapters.summary: Epilogue, eighteen months later. Yara, released, works quietly auditing small nonprofits—clean money, honestly dirty paperwork. They visit a meadow above the Alps where the flight last pinged, plant nothing, promise nothing. Final line: staying invisible was never really an option; being seen, finally, is enough.
